name: Dali Thoy
subtitle: the everyday konkani toor dal, thin and clean, finished with hing and green chilli

ingredients.note: not strictly traditional but common in Mangalore homes
the flavour of this dal is really coconut oil and hing, so use both properly
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Rinse the toor dal until the water runs clear. Cloudy dal makes a muddy thoy.
No soaking needed, but 20 minutes in warm water shaves cooking time if you are in a hurry.
Have the tempering ingredients within reach of the stove; the whole tadka takes under a minute.

steps.text: Pressure cook the dal with 2 1/2 cups water and the turmeric for 4 whistles, then let the pressure fall on its own.
Open the cooker and whisk the dal smooth, adding up to 1/2 cup hot water. Thoy should pour like thin cream, not sit in a mound.
steps.tip: This is the single thing people get wrong. Thoy is meant to be thin enough to drink from the bowl.

steps.text: Add the green chillies, crushed ginger and salt and simmer 5 minutes on low.
Taste and check the salt now, while there is still time for it to dissolve evenly.
Heat the coconut oil in a small pan until it shimmers, then add the mustard seeds and let them pop fully, about 20 seconds.
steps.tip: Wait for the popping to actually stop. Half-popped mustard tastes raw and slightly bitter.

steps.text: Take the pan off the flame, add the broken red chilli, curry leaves and hing, and let them foam in the residual heat for 5 seconds.
steps.tip: Hing burns almost instantly on a live flame. Off the heat is the only safe way.

steps.text: Pour the tempering into the dal, cover immediately and leave it 2 minutes to trap the aroma.
Stir through the coriander leaves and serve hot over rice with a spoon of coconut oil and a piece of pickle.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. It thickens in the fridge, so whisk in hot water and re-warm gently; the tempering flattens after a day, so a fresh 20-second tadka on top is worth it.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Ingredients given to taste rather than by weight are counted as zero, so the real figure is a little higher than this. The + says so.
